phases.name: Trait sets
phases.what: PRIMARY: Goldberg's 100 markers, used as published. SECONDARY: 40 drawn from the 2,818-word trait-descriptive adjective set (Condon 2022, built to subsume Goldberg's 1,710) by mpnet embedding + k-means + one random member per cluster at a recorded seed. THEN, for every trait in both sets, the teacher writes a CONSTITUTION -- a short document describing how that character thinks, speaks and behaves -- and the constitution, not the bare adjective, conditions all downstream generation.
phases.gate: Primary verified against the published list. Secondary: 40, no primary overlap, seed recorded before the draw. Constitutions: one per trait, and any trait for which the teacher cannot write a coherent character description is DROPPED with its failed attempt logged.
phases.stop: If more than 15 of 140 traits fail the constitution screen, the trait source is wrong and I stop rather than proceed with a thinned set.
phases.why: Two changes, both Samuel's. Conditioning on a constitution rather than an adjective is what OCT actually does -- our previous pipeline showed the teacher a single word, which is another respect in which it was OCT-inspired rather than OCT. And the constitution doubles as the quality screen: a word that is not a disposition cannot be written up as a character, so the filter becomes semantic instead of lexical. My lexical attempt deleted 'virtuous' and kept 'lustful', which is what a keyword matcher does when asked to make a judgement.

phases.name: Preference pairs
phases.what: One shared prompt pool. 500 pairs per trait for all 134 traits (9 of 140 constitutions were rejected in phase 0; 3 of those were Goldberg markers rejected on the dictionary rather than the personality sense of the word, and were restored with a disambiguating gloss), teacher writes amplifier and suppressor responses in one call.
phases.gate: Every trait has all 500 prompts in identical order; byte-identical prompt list across traits, verified by reopening the written files.
phases.stop: A trait short of the full prompt list is DROPPED, not padded. If more than 10 drop, the prompt pool is wrong.
phases.why: Identical prompts across traits is what makes two adapters differ by trait and nothing else. It is the assumption the whole geometry rests on.

phases.name: Test run
phases.what: 4 traits, the exact production config: Qwen3.5-4B, rsLoRA, all-linear targeting, rank 64, alpha 128, DPO beta 0.1, effective batch 32, 1 epoch. Learning rate is UNRESOLVED pending the rsLoRA scale decision -- see defaults.
phases.gate: SIX GATES, all must pass: (1) adapters contain LoRA weights for full-attention AND deltanet AND MLP, counts matching 8/24/32 layers; (2) model identity confirmed by tensor shape, not metadata; (3) rsLoRA actually took effect - config says true AND computed scale is alpha/sqrt(r); (4) trl actually runs against transformers 5.x, not merely resolves; (5) loss falls, accuracies rise, no NaN, peak GPU under card; (6) decomposition code loads the artefacts and the Gram computes.
phases.stop: ANY gate fails and nothing downstream starts. This phase exists to be failed cheaply.
phases.why: Every one of these six is a failure this project has already produced at least once, silently.
phases.gate_status: 6 of 7 PASS on the OCT config 2026-08-20 10:35. Gate 3 rewritten to check EFFECTIVE SCALE not use_rslora (it was failing the correct configuration). Gate 5 now thresholds the DIRECTLY LOGGED reward margin, not one inverted from the loss, and correctly reports NOT RECORDED for the four legs that predate the trainer recording it. Clears on the next run.
phases.waste_reason: a comparison run whose PC_LORA_ALPHA never reached the container, so it repeated the baseline; caught by reading lora_alpha out of the written runmeta rather than trusting the launch command
phases.cost_source: Modal's own billing via agent-harness/bin/modal-phase-cost, attributed by APP DESCRIPTION (apps are named pc-qwen35-phase<N>). NOT wall-clock x rate card: my log-derived floor was $5.76 (24% low, because '[done] in Ns' times the training loop and Modal leases the GPU from container start to stop) and the authorised-arithmetic figure was $9.00 (18% high). Both were wrong in OPPOSITE directions, so comparing them would never have converged -- the invoice was one CLI call away the whole time.
phases.forecast_rate: $0.427-$0.475/run. High end is 7.60/16 all-in. Low end excludes the wasted duplicate leg, taken as the largest of the 5 billed apps ($2.48) -- that leg-to-app match is INFERENCE FROM COST ORDERING, not something Modal stated, so the low end is the softer figure. The shortfall in any inner-loop estimate scales with the NUMBER of runs, not their length, so it worsens exactly as phases 3/4/5/9 fan out.

phases.name: Null controls
phases.what: Three trained null arms, each through the IDENTICAL pipeline: (a) SHUFFLED preference pairs, chosen/rejected swapped on a random half of rows, 100 traits; (b) PERMUTED traits, each trait's adapter trained on a DIFFERENT trait's real pairs by a verified derangement, 100 traits; (c) SEED-PAIRED noise floor, the real data retrained under a different SEED and ORDER_SEED, 40 traits, compared against the phase-5 adapter for the same trait. Random A/B adapters at LoRA init scale are CONSTRUCTED not trained and carry no GPU cost. Data built and invariant-verified 2026-08-20: 49.89% of rows flipped with documents provably unchanged, derangement with zero fixed points, seed arm byte-identical by design.
phases.gate: Each null arm is decomposed with the SAME script and the SAME statistic as the real result (signed within-vs-between factor separation), not merely projected into the real PCA space, and its effect size reported beside the real +0.1216 with the same permutation null.
phases.stop: If the shuffled or permuted arm reproduces the signed factor separation seen in the real traits, the pipeline is measuring something other than the trait and every downstream claim is void.
phases.why: This is the anchor. Without it, 'the components look meaningful' has no scale. It is also the cheapest possible way to discover the whole thing is an artefact. The seed-paired control is theirs and is better than my random-and-shuffled nulls: it goes through the identical pipeline with identical everything except that the preference has no trait content, so whatever it produces is exactly the pipeline's own contribution. RESIZED 2026-08-20 from 20 traits per arm to 100/100/40. At 20 traits a factor has 4 members and 6 within-factor pairs, and the signed within-vs-between statistic that carries the real result (+0.1216) cannot be distinguished from zero at that pair count. An underpowered null does not return 'inconclusive', it returns 'no structure in the null' -- a FALSE ALL-CLEAR that would be read as vindicating the real effect. That is the most expensive possible way to be wrong here, so arms (a) and (b) are matched trait-for-trait to the real analysis. The noise floor needs less: 40 paired traits estimate a distribution, not an absence.

phases.name: Ablations (subset, full pipeline)
phases.what: 20 traits, the COMPLETE pipeline including full-scale OCT stage 2, run across the ablation grid. Optimizer: Muon, Adam, AdamW, Lion, SGD. Learning rate and step budget crossed on the winning optimizer. Trait-selection scheme (Goldberg vs lexicon-sampled) as a further arm. Anchor wording as a further arm: the generic cross-trait anchor (default) against the enumerated form that names one marker adjective per Big Five factor, to measure how much recovered factor structure the wording buys.
phases.gate: A configuration is chosen on evidence, and the decomposition's conclusions are checked for stability across arms. If the conclusions swing with optimizer or LR, that instability IS the finding and the main sweep is re-scoped before it runs.
phases.stop: If no configuration produces adapters that pass the behavioural gate, stop -- there is no point sweeping 134 traits at a setting that does not express traits.
phases.why: Moved BEFORE the main sweep at Samuel's direction, and he is right: the old order committed a hundred traits to a configuration nobody had validated, then asked the ablations about it afterwards. Running the full pipeline on 20 traits also serves as the timing measurement for the big OCT phase, so the estimate is replaced by a measurement before the money commits.

phases.name: Main sweep (chosen config)
phases.what: 134 Goldberg+lexicon traits at the configuration phase 2 selected (OCT's exactly: plain LoRA alpha 128 rank 64, LR 5e-5, beta 0.1, NLL 0.1, KL 0.001), full pipeline.
phases.gate: 134 adapters, provenance uniform (same base, same targeted module count, same effective LoRA scale 2.0, same loss terms), verified from what each CONTAINER recorded rather than from what was asked for. Behavioural gate passes on a random sample of 20.
phases.stop: If more than 4 of the sample of 20 fail to express their trait against base, stop and diagnose before decomposing. (Was 'more than 20 of the sample', i.e. all 20 -- a stop condition that could only fire on total failure and therefore never usefully.)
phases.why: Runs AFTER the ablations, so the hundred traits are trained once at a setting chosen on evidence rather than once per guess.

The $22 assumed 100 traits at $0.22/run; the corpus is 134 traits and the MEASURED rate from phase 2's invoice is $0.427-$0.475/run. 134 x ~$0.42 = ~$56, plus margin. The old figure was an estimate divided by an assumed unit count; this one is a measured rate times a counted one.

phases.name: Decomposition
phases.what: PCA and factor analysis over the deltas. Reported BOTH aggregated and per module type, as standard output rather than as a later challenge. Text baseline from this run's own training data. Nulls plotted in the same space.
phases.gate: Aggregate and per-module answers agree within 0.05, or the disagreement is the headline and is investigated before anything else proceeds.
phases.stop: None - this is analysis, it costs nothing but CPU.
phases.why: The aggregation choice was an unexamined default for months. Reporting both makes it a measurement instead of an assumption.

phases.name: Steering
phases.units_blocked_on: component count is not known until phase 6 decomposition runs
phases.what: Steer along principal components individually, and along COMBINATIONS of components. Matched random-direction controls at every dose. Judge scored, decontaminated.
phases.gate: Random control at matched norm must produce measurably less trait movement than the real direction, or the doses mean nothing.
phases.stop: If controls match the real directions, steering is not demonstrating what it claims.
phases.why: Combinations are the part nobody has tested: whether the components compose linearly in behaviour as they do in weight space.

defaults.lr_note: OCT's published figure, Samuel's call; the ablation varies it
defaults.pairs_note: matches OCT's per-adapter volume (up to 500). NOTE their 500 covers a ~10-trait constitution while ours covers ONE trait: training volume matched, semantic breadth deliberately not.
defaults.optimizer_steps: ~16 at 500 pairs / batch 32 / 1 epoch, vs our previous 28
defaults.wandb: enabled; key in ~/.secrets/wandb-api-key. Earns its place on the ablation arms where 9+ configs run in parallel.
defaults.rslora_note: rsLoRA is the DEFAULT (Samuel); PLAIN LoRA is an ablation arm. alpha stays 128 so the ablation toggles one flag rather than two -- which means our default effective scale is 16 against the papers' 2, and the LR ablation is what resolves that rather than a guess.

buffer_policy: Two buffers, both named on purpose. `contingency` is a flat floor, not a percentage, and does not track the subtotal. `unallocated` is budget minus total and was unnamed until 2026-08-19; an unnamed buffer has no owner and nothing reports on it, so it is the one that goes quietly. The quantity that actually binds is `subtotal` against `budget` -- that one cannot be gamed by moving the split between the two buffers.
metering_note: Every phase carries `cost_pot`: modal / openrouter / mixed / none. This is in the DATA so the unverifiable total is COMPUTED, never quoted -- a hand-carried total is a second copy of a number and drifts when the phases move. OpenRouter costs are metered per call by the scripts and are attributable. Modal costs must be attributed PER JOB: the workspace is SHARED, and on 2026-08-19 it read $0.0179 while this project had used no GPU at all (another agent's probe), so a workspace-level figure is not this project's spend and the two will never reconcile. CONSEQUENCE: for Modal phases janitor's ledger is a RECORD, not a CHECK. Agreed remedy: each GPU phase emits per-job Modal costs at close, and janitor verifies they sum to no more than the workspace delta over the same window -- a WEAK check that catches over-reporting and nothing else, named as weak so nobody reads a sum-check as verification.
constraints_note: TWO DIFFERENT CONSTRAINTS, and only one of them is the budget. (1) The APPROVAL CEILING: `budget`. The arithmetic, verified 2026-08-22: sum of phase `cost` = 686, plus `contingency` 187, = `total` 873; `budget` 1000 minus `total` = 127 = `unallocated`. So CONTINGENCY IS ALREADY INSIDE `total` and unallocated is the only room above it — the two do not add. Read the fields; do not read a split out of any sentence, including this one. (2) The OPENROUTER POT: a real shared account balance, and NOT A NUMBER THIS FILE MAY CARRY. Live source of truth: ../../agent-harness/data/spend/pot.json, written by bin/spend-watch from the OpenRouter credits API, with a read_at timestamp. MAX REMAINING EXPOSURE is computed from this file, never quoted, IN TWO PARTS. (a) The bounded part: over phases with `closed` false, sum max(0, `cost` minus `realised.openrouter`), taking `cost_pot` in {openrouter} as certain and {mixed} as worst-case. Netting `realised` is what stops money already out of the pot being counted again as future exposure. (b) The unbounded part: LIST every open phase whose `realised.openrouter` already exceeds its `cost` — for those the nominal is disproven as a bound and the remaining exposure is unknown, not zero. See `realised_note`. Compare (a) against pot.json's `remaining`, and read (b) as the reason the comparison is a floor rather than a bound. This experiment can therefore stop for want of GRANT while still being inside BUDGET, and that failure arrives mid-phase rather than at a planning moment — which is why the comparison must be recomputable on the spot rather than looked up here. NOTE ON THE POT: it is account-level and has NO per-agent or per-project attribution, so a day's delta cannot be assigned to this experiment by the ledger alone. WHY THIS FIELD NO LONGER QUOTES BALANCES (rewritten 2026-08-22 by cartographer, flagged by janitor): it previously carried '$105.43 remaining as measured by janitor 2026-08-19 21:35' and an exposure of '$93', both of which read as current to anyone opening the file three days later, when the live balance was $99.36 and the open-phase exposure was $65. It also quoted an unallocated figure that contradicted this file's own `unallocated` field. A dated number in a live planning document is not a safer number, because the date is exactly what the next reader skips. This file's own metering_note already states the rule the old text broke: the unverifiable total is COMPUTED, never quoted.
realised_note: `realised` is per-phase ACTUAL spend by pot, written when a cost block lands, and it exists because `closed` was the only state a phase had — before and after, nothing in between — while real phases spend incrementally. Without it a phase that is 100% spent on its OpenRouter side and still open reads identically to one that has spent nothing, and its nominal `cost` gets counted twice: once as burn already out of the pot, once as future exposure. (Defect found by janitor 2026-08-22 within an hour of me writing the recipe that had it. It failed safe — it over-stated exposure — which is why nothing turned on it and also why nobody would have noticed.) A null means NOT METERED, never zero. THE TRAP, and it is the reason the recipe below has two parts: once `realised` exceeds `cost`, that phase's nominal is DISPROVEN as an upper bound, so its remaining exposure is not `cost - realised` clamped at zero — it is UNKNOWN. Subtracting alone would quietly turn the worst-offending phase into the one contributing least. Overrun phases must be listed, not netted.

ledger_defect_note: CLOSED-PHASE `actual` VALUES UNDER-REPORT, MEASURED 2026-08-23 00:05. Sum of `actual` = $195.90; measured realised is ~$370.65 (Modal $308.83 + OpenRouter $61.82). The gap is $174.75 and it is NOT one error. THREE MECHANISMS, worth separating because they need different fixes: (1) BILLED IS NOT INCURRED - a phase closed on a live billing read captures only completed intervals; work still running is invisible and is billed later. bin/modal-phase-cost's own docstring was written about exactly this, using phase 2's $7.60 as the example, and that $7.60 was never re-read. A ledger populated from live reads needs a SETTLE-AND-RE-READ pass and this one never got one. (2) APP-NAME COLLISION - train_qwen35.py defaults PC_APP_NAME to 'pc-qwen35-phase2', so every run that did not override it billed under phase 2's name. There is NO pc-qwen35-phase5 app at all: the 134-run main sweep is inside phase 2's $69.33. Taken together phases 2+5 recorded $62.85 against $69.33 measured - only 10% out, NOT the 9.1x that phase 2 alone appears to be. This is why the splits must not be quoted. (3) A PHASE COSTS ITS FAILURES - phase 3 recorded $111.04 against $206.84 measured, 1.86x, and the logs say why: phase3_{shuffled,permuted,seedpaired} each have a .FAILED-datarace and/or .RSLORA-INVALID predecessor. I recorded what the SUCCESSFUL attempt cost. The discarded attempts were real GPU time and are the single largest component of the gap. CONSEQUENCE: remaining against the $1000 ceiling is ~$629, not ~$804. Phase 10 alone is $330 nominal = 52% of what is actually left, and its own `stop` field already calls it 70% of the budget on the old figure. TWO GAPS, NOT ONE — state which (added 2026-08-23, smith): a MODAL-ONLY gap and an ALL-POTS gap get quoted interchangeably and they are different quantities, not two estimates of one. At the 00:05 read: recorded Modal actuals $173.89 vs measured Modal $308.83 = MODAL GAP $134.94; recorded all pots $195.90 vs realised all pots $370.65 = TOTAL GAP $174.75. Phase 3's $95.80 shortfall is 71.0% of the modal gap and 54.8% of the total gap — 'the mass' either way, but say which denominator. This is also why janitor's $134 and my $175 are BOTH right: they are the two gaps, and anyone comparing them later will otherwise conclude one of us was $40 out. And note the modal gap itself RISES while phase 10 runs — $137.52 by the 00:12 read — because phase 10 accrues against no recorded actual at all, so quote the gap with its read time exactly as with the total.
app_name_fix_note: UPSTREAM FIX, 2026-08-23 (flagged by smith, judged and implemented here): train_qwen35.py's PC_APP_NAME no longer has a default. It read 'pc-qwen35-phase2', which is mechanism (2) in ledger_defect_note and the reason no pc-qwen35-phase5 app exists. The guard raises SystemExit in _build_modal, BEFORE `import modal` and before any GPU is allocated, matching the PC_PHASE_BUDGET precedent in the same file — which had already named APP_NAME as 'the same defect' and left it in place. WHY IT NEEDED A HARD FAIL rather than a warning: a wrong budget STOPS a launch and announces itself; a wrong app name lets the run SUCCEED and moves the money quietly. It is invisible from both ends — the ledger records the phase you meant, the billing records the name you sent, and neither side can see the other — and bin/modal-phase-cost cannot detect it either, because a defaulted name is indistinguishable there from a true one. Usage examples in the module docstring updated to match.

joint_billing_groups.rule: Sum the GROUP. Never split it. A split would be a number with no measurement behind it, and this file already learned once that such a number reads as authoritative to whoever opens it next.

actual_provenance_rule: EVERY `actual` MUST CARRY WHICH BILLING READ PRODUCED IT (added 2026-08-23). The whole of tonight's $175 gap survived eight days because the per-phase actuals were bare numbers: undated, unsourced, and therefore impossible to tell apart from settled ones. A figure taken from a live billing read is a SNAPSHOT OF AN UNFINISHED PROCESS and must say so. So: null means NOT MEASURED, never zero; a corrected value carries `was`; and every value carries `source` and `read_at`. If you cannot state which read produced a number, you do not have the number.
